title_tag: Jobber Review (2026): Honest Pricing, Pros & Cons
title: Jobber: The Best First Software for a Small Shop
meta: Honest Jobber review for contractors in 2026: real pricing (Core to Plus), what it does well (quoting, scheduling, invoicing, CRM), where it costs you (per-user fees, gated features), and who should actually buy it.
dek: Not every tool sold to you is a scam. Jobber is the one most small shops should actually run — quote, schedule, invoice, and get paid from one app your crew can use without a training weekend. Here's the honest cost and the catch.
verdict_text: For a solo-to-mid crew, yes. Jobber is the cleanest all-in-one for quoting, scheduling, invoicing, and CRM, it's genuinely easy, and it scores high on user satisfaction. The catch: extra users run ~$29/mo each and some features are gated to pricier tiers, so price the plan for the crew you have. Start on the free trial, not the top plan.

blocks.html: Jobber is a field-service operating system for home-service businesses: quoting, scheduling and dispatch, invoicing, payments, and a client CRM, in one web + mobile app. It replaces the clipboard, the text-message schedule, and the “I'll invoice you later” that never happens. For a one-to-fifteen-person shop it's the most common honest answer to “what software should I use?” — and it's a real tool, not a lead mill renting you your own customers.

faq.q: Is Jobber worth it for a small contractor?
faq.a: For most solo-to-mid crews, yes. It brings quoting, scheduling, invoicing, payments, and CRM into one easy app and scores high on user satisfaction. Start on Core or Connect and a free trial; only move up tiers when the added features clearly pay for themselves.

faq.q: How much does Jobber cost in 2026?
faq.a: Roughly $29–$49/mo for Core (1 user), ~$99–$139 for Connect (up to 5), ~$149–$199 for Grow (up to 10), and ~$399–$499 for Plus (up to 15), billed month-to-month; annual billing saves about 25–40%. Extra users are ~$29/mo each. Confirm current pricing on getjobber.com.

Jobber tends to win on price, ease of use, and customer-facing CRM and is the better starting point for small crews. Housecall Pro offers more breadth and built-in financing tools but costs more. See our side-by-side comparison.
